misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must always be wrapped in if/else statements to be returned as Boolean values.

solutions.generated_code:
program SaringKataPanjang
kamus
  n, m, i, panjangKata : integer
  kata : string
  cukupPanjang : boolean
algoritma
  input(n, m)
  for i <- 1 to m do
    input(kata)
    panjangKata <- panjang(kata)
    if panjangKata > n then
      cukupPanjang <- true
    else
      cukupPanjang <- false
    endif
    if cukupPanjang then
      output(kata)
    endif
  endfor
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes they need to wrap the boolean expression `len(x) > n` in an if/else statement to get a boolean value for `is_long`, rather than directly assigning `is_long = len(x) > n`. This makes the code more verbose but doesn't change its correctness. The student genuinely believes this is the proper way to convert a conditional expression into a boolean variable that can be used later.
